extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and writers seeking classical guidance on writing and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing poetry and for practicing fair, informed literary criticism grounded in classical principles (Horace, Aristotle, Longinus, Quintilian). Emphasizes taste, modesty, method, and the character of a good critic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain censure; prefer silence to spite
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Tis best sometimes your censure to restrain, And charitably let the dull be vain; Your silence there is better than your spite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not feel obliged to attack every poor work; when criticism would be merely spiteful or repetitive, silence is the kinder and wiser choice. Excessive railing only perpetuates bad writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not feed bad writers by prolonged railing
rubrics_metrics.description: For who can rail so long as they can write? ... False steps but help them to renew the race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent, public denunciation can sustain or encourage trivial writers; prolonged attention may simply motivate more output from them. Consider the effects of criticism on the production it addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid empty sound and jingling syllables
rubrics_metrics.description: What crowds of these, impenitently bold, In sounds and jingling syllables grown old, ... Strain out the last dull droppings of their sense, And rhyme with all the rage of impotence!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should avoid mere ornament or forced rhyme that lacks sense. Prioritize sense and authentic expression over mechanical or showy versifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be a 'bookful blockhead'—avoid rote learning without understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The bookful blockhead ignorantly read, With loads of learned lumber in his head, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic should not substitute accumulation of quotations or learned trivia for genuine understanding. Knowledge must be assimilated and used judiciously, not paraded as authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prejudiced, blanket criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: All books he reads and all he reads assails ... With him most authors steal their works or buy;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should not assume every author is guilty of theft or error; avoid sweeping denunciations and unfair generalizations. Be specific and justified in accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't be a mere sycophant or superficial friend to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Name a new play, and he's the poet's friend; Nay, showed his faults--but when would poets mend?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should not automatically praise new works out of friendliness nor avoid honest correction; effective criticism balances praise and correction to encourage improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise modest caution; distrustful sense speaks modestly
rubrics_metrics.description: Distrustful sense with modest caution speaks, It still looks home, and short excursions makes;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound judgment is modest and cautious. Good criticism avoids grandiloquent pronouncements and prefers careful, measured observations rooted in experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rattling, bombastic nonsense
rubrics_metrics.description: But rattling nonsense in full volleys breaks, And, never shocked, and never turned aside. Bursts out, resistless, with a thundering tide,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showy, loud, unreasoned criticism (or writing) that overwhelms with noise rather than argument is to be avoided; clarity and restraint are preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be able to teach while remaining willing to learn
rubrics_metrics.description: But where's the man who counsel can bestow, Still pleased to teach, and yet not proud to know?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal critic is both instructive and humble—ready to give counsel but also open to correction and further learning; pride hinders honest judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbiased judgment: not swayed by favor or spite
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbiased, or by favor, or in spite, Not dully prepossessed, nor blindly right;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism must be impartial—neither corrupted by favoritism nor driven by personal spite. Avoid preconceptions and evaluate on merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modestly bold and humanly severe — candid but fair correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Though learned, well-bred, and though well bred, sincere, Modestly bold, and humanly severe, Who to a friend his faults can freely show, And gladly praise the merit of a foe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should be courageous enough to point out faults (even to friends) but humane and fair; they should also be ready to acknowledge excellence in those they oppose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste exact yet unconfined; knowledge of books and mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Blessed with a taste exact, yet unconfined; A knowledge both of books and human kind;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good critical taste is precise without being narrow; it combines literary learning with an understanding of human nature and social context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love to praise where reason warrants it
rubrics_metrics.description: And love to praise, with reason on his side?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good critic should be disposed to praise when merited and base praise on rational grounds rather than sentiment or faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority should come from demonstrated mastery (Aristotelian ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mighty Stagirite ... He steered securely, and discovered far, Led by the light of the Maeonian star. ... Who conquered nature, should preside o'er wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who have mastered the art (conquered nature) and demonstrated understanding are best qualified to set rules and judge others; theoretical pronouncement should be grounded in practice and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horatian ideal: graceful negligence and clear, friendly conveyance of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Horace still charms with graceful negligence, And without method talks us into sense; Will like a friend familiarly convey The truest notions in the easiest way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style that seems effortless and conversational can most effectively communicate truth; critics and writers should favor clarity, naturalness, and accessibility in expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic should judge with coolness though write with fire
rubrics_metrics.description: He who supreme in judgment as in wit, Might boldly censure, as he boldly writ, Yet judged with coolness though he sung with fire;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow passion in creative work but maintain calm, balanced judgment in criticism. Let the vigor of poetry not undermine measured critical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the hypocrisy of harsh judges who write poorly
rubrics_metrics.description: Our critics take a contrary extreme: They judge with fury, but they write with phlegm:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should avoid condemning with excessive heat if their own writing lacks comparable excellence; authority is weakened by inconsistency between judgment and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine and elicit beauties from texts (Dionysius/Longinus model)
rubrics_metrics.description: See Dionysius Homer's thoughts refine, And call new beauties forth from every line! ... Thee bold Longinus! ... An ardent judge, who, zealous in his trust, With warmth gives sentence, yet is always just: Whose own example strengthens all his laws;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should illuminate and bring out latent qualities in a text, not merely fault-find. An ardent but just critic whose own practice exemplifies his standards is most persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine scholarship with ease; clear method and useful rules (Quintilian/Petronius)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fancy and art in gay Petronius please, The scholar's learning with the courtier's ease. In grave Quintilian's copious work we find The justest rules and clearest method joined:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good critical writing marries learning with accessibility; theory should supply clear, practical rules and methods useful for practice rather than pedantic obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repress license; ordain useful rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus long succeeding critics justly reigned, License repressed, and useful laws ordained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the critic's role is to check excessive license in art and to establish useful, practical standards that preserve craft and quality.
